title: Find tickets
purpose: Find a ticket or a client organization from one search box: a ticket's number, words in its subject, the organization, contact or caller, a reference, an identifier from a linked record, or an organization's name, account code, email, phone or city.
summary: Use the top bar search, Find on the phone navigation bar, or Find on the Tickets list. A ticket number opens the ticket. Other searches list matching tickets and client organizations.

tasks.title: Open a ticket by its number
steps: Type the number, such as REQ-000123, in the search box and select [[Find]]. The ticket opens.

tasks.title: Find a ticket from what a caller said
steps: Type part of an organization or contact name, the caller's name, a subject word or a reference number and select [[Find]].
Open a ticket with its number in the Results table.

tasks.title: Find tickets linked to a requisition, order or sample
steps: Type the identifier from the requisition, order or sample and select [[Find]]. Matching tickets show A linked record under Found by.

good_to_know: Typing only digits, such as 123, opens the ticket with that number when you may read it.
You only find tickets you may read. A restricted ticket never appears for someone outside its team who is not a supervisor.
Find returns up to 50 tickets and 20 organizations. Enter a more specific term to narrow either list. Use the Tickets list to filter tickets by status, team or assignee.

sections.title: Search
paragraphs: Any active staff role may use this page. Client portal accounts cannot. The page is at the address ending /requests/find/.

items.label: Ticket number, organization, name, reference or identifier
items.description: The search box, up to 200 characters as typed; longer text is refused with a message under the box, and nothing is searched. Spaces at either end are then ignored. A ticket number (with or without REQ- and leading zeros) that exists and that you may read opens that ticket directly. Otherwise the text is matched, ignoring case, against the number, subject, organization name and account code, contact name, the caller's name (Reported by) and the reference given. When links to orders, samples and other records exist, a matching identifier lists every ticket that carries the link. Searches by patient, participant or donor keys are for staff with the patient capability only, and are matched exactly.

items.label: Find
items.description: Runs the search. The address keeps your text, so the result can be bookmarked.

items.label: Number
items.description: Results column. The ticket number; it opens the ticket.

items.label: Status
items.description: Results column. Open, Waiting on client, Waiting on third party, Resolved or Closed.

items.label: Organization
items.description: Results column. The client organization, or No organization.

items.label: Found by
items.description: Results column. A linked record when the match came from an identifier on a link, otherwise Its details.

items.label: Nothing found
items.description: Shown when nothing matches. Check the number or try part of a name.

sections.title: Client organizations
paragraphs: The Client organizations table matches the search against organization name, account code, email, phone and city.

items.label: Account code
items.description: The laboratory’s code for the organization. A dash means there is no recorded code.

items.label: Status
items.description: Shows whether the organization is active or inactive.

items.label: City
items.description: The city in the organization’s address. A dash means there is no recorded city.

items.label: No organization matches
items.description: Try part of the name, account code, email, phone number or city.

items.label: Restricted tickets
items.description: Results, the number shortcut and identifier matches all start from the tickets you may read. Tickets in a restricted category are included only for members of the ticket's team and for supervisors. The number of a ticket you may not read does not open it.

items.label: Result size and order
items.description: Up to 50 tickets appear in order of most recent activity. Up to 20 organizations appear with active organizations first, then by name. Neither table has pagination.
